question: A 5-year-old male visits his pediatrician for a check-up. His height corresponds to the 99th percentile for his age, and pubic hair is present upon physical examination. Serum renin and potassium levels are high, as is 17-hydroxyprogesterone. Which of the following is likely deficient in this patient?

paths: (Deficiency of steroid 21-monooxygenase)-ISA->(Symptoms)-MANIFESTATION_OF->(voltage gated channel)-ASSOCIATED_WITH->(Oligomeric Procyanidin Complex)

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: High serum renin and potassium levels -> increased 17-hydroxyprogesterone -> likely 21-hydroxylase deficiency -> opc. 21-hydroxylase -> 95%
enhanced_information: High serum renin and potassium levels, along with elevated 17-hydroxyprogesterone, suggest likely 21-hydroxylase deficiency in this patient. This aligns with the consensus that 21-hydroxylase deficiency leads to increased 17-hydroxyprogesterone levels. The evidence paths support this by linking 17-hydroxyprogesterone to 21-hydroxylase deficiency. Therefore, opc. 21-hydroxylase is likely deficient in this case.
analysis: The presentation of high serum renin and potassium levels, along with elevated 17-hydroxyprogesterone, strongly suggests 21-hydroxylase deficiency in this patient. 21-hydroxylase deficiency is a common cause of congenital adrenal hyperplasia, leading to impaired cortisol and aldosterone synthesis, resulting in increased androgen production. The clinical findings of precocious puberty (pubic hair development) and tall stature align with this diagnosis.
